```{=html}
<style>
.ll-pick{display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:.4rem;margin:1rem 0 1.4rem}
.ll-pick button{font-family:var(--font-mono);font-size:.82rem;padding:.35rem .8rem;border:1px solid var(--site-border);border-radius:999px;background:var(--site-surface);color:var(--site-ink)}
.ll-pick button[aria-pressed="true"]{background:var(--site-accent-dk);border-color:var(--site-accent-dk);color:#fff}
.ll-pick button:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--site-accent-dk);outline-offset:2px}
.ll-list{display:grid;gap:.8rem;padding:0;margin:0;list-style:none}
.ll-list li{border:1px solid var(--site-border);border-radius:8px;background:var(--site-surface);padding:.9rem 1.1rem}
.ll-list li[hidden]{display:none}
.ll-list a{font-family:var(--font-display);font-size:1.2rem;font-weight:600;text-decoration:none}

.ll-list p{margin:.3rem 0 0;color:var(--site-ink-2)}

</style>

<p>The site's backing band plays every example in these lessons. Choose an instrument, a topic, or both. They run roughly from simpler to more involved.</p>

<div class="ll-pick" id="ll-pick" role="group" aria-label="Instrument">
  <button type="button" data-inst="all">All</button>
  <button type="button" data-inst="bass">Bass</button>
  <button type="button" data-inst="guitar">Guitar</button>
  <button type="button" data-inst="piano">Piano</button>
  <button type="button" data-inst="drums">Drums</button>
  <button type="button" data-inst="congas">Congas</button>
  <button type="button" data-inst="violin">Violin</button>
  <button type="button" data-inst="sax">Saxophone</button>
  <button type="button" data-inst="voice">Voice</button>
  <button type="button" data-inst="other">Another instrument</button>
</div>
<div class="ll-pick" id="ll-topic" role="group" aria-label="Topic">
  <button type="button" data-topic="all">Any topic</button>
  <button type="button" data-topic="blues">Blues</button>
  <button type="button" data-topic="jazz">Jazz</button>
  <button type="button" data-topic="pop">Pop</button>
  <button type="button" data-topic="latin">Latin</button>
  <button type="button" data-topic="harmony">Harmony</button>
  <button type="button" data-topic="rhythm">Rhythm</button>
  <button type="button" data-topic="improv">Improvising</button>
  <button type="button" data-topic="reading">Reading</button>
  <button type="button" data-topic="sound">Sound and synths</button>
</div>
<p class="ll-note" id="ll-note" aria-live="polite" hidden>No lessons match both choices yet.</p>

<ul class="ll-list" id="ll-list">
  <li data-for="all bass guitar piano violin sax other" data-topic="blues jazz improv">
    <a href="blues-improv.html">Improvising on a Blues: Blues in the Closet</a>
    <p>Starting from the melody: hitting the change in bar 5, the blues and pentatonic scales, and a scale for each chord. Scales are shown as tablature, keyboard fingerings or a violin fingerboard, whichever you play.</p>
  </li>
  <li data-for="all violin sax other" data-topic="blues jazz reading">
    <a href="blues-melody.html">Blues for Violin and Saxophone: Playing the Changes</a>
    <p>For any instrument that plays one note at a time. Roots, chord tones, guide-tone lines, a riff, and the melody of <em>Blues in the Closet</em>, written in your own key.</p>
  </li>
  <li data-for="all bass guitar piano drums violin sax other" data-topic="blues jazz harmony">
    <a href="blues-changes.html">Changing the Changes in a 12-Bar Blues</a>
    <p>What the chords of a blues are and how players vary them, from three chords to a jazz blues, with a chorus you can build yourself and an ear test.</p>
  </li>
  <li data-for="all bass" data-topic="blues jazz harmony reading">
    <a href="blues-bass.html">Blues for Bass: From Roots to a Walking Line</a>
    <p>Roots, then root and fifth, then the chord tones as a written line, then walking. Fretboard diagrams, bass-clef notation and the band's own bass line written out.</p>
  </li>
  <li data-for="all guitar" data-topic="blues jazz harmony">
    <a href="blues-guitar.html">Blues for Guitar: From Roots to Shell Chords</a>
    <p>Two- and three-note chords built from the 3rd and 7th, on strings 5 and 4 and on strings 4 and 3, with the same shapes a tritone higher. No barre chords.</p>
  </li>
  <li data-for="all piano" data-topic="blues jazz harmony">
    <a href="blues-piano.html">Blues for Piano: From Roots to Rootless Voicings</a>
    <p>Left-hand roots, guide tones in the right hand, three-note shells and rootless left-hand voicings, each on a keyboard diagram and a grand staff.</p>
  </li>
  <li data-for="all drums" data-topic="blues jazz rhythm reading">
    <a href="blues-drums.html">Blues for Drums: From Quarter Notes to the Shuffle</a>
    <p>How to read a drum part, then the beat, the ride pattern, swing time, fills that mark the form, the shuffle, the slow 12/8 and straight eighths.</p>
  </li>
  <li data-for="all bass guitar piano drums violin sax other" data-topic="jazz rhythm reading">
    <a href="reading-swing.html">Reading Swing from a Lead Sheet</a>
    <p>Why swing eighths are written as plain eighths, how far the long-short can stretch with tempo and style, and the range of good readings, with <em>Blues in the Closet</em> swung and <em>Watermelon Man</em> straight for contrast. Every example plays, with a swing slider.</p>
  </li>
  <li data-for="all drums" data-topic="rhythm">
    <a href="hihat-grooves.html">Hi-Hat Grooves: From Quarter Notes to Sixteenths</a>
    <p>For a drummer who can already play a basic beat. The three sounds of the hi-hat, then quarter notes, eighths, accents, off-beats, an open note, open off-beats, sixteenths with one hand and with two, the foot alone and the swing hi-hat.</p>
  </li>
  <li data-for="all congas" data-topic="latin rhythm reading">
    <a href="congas-basics.html">How to Play Congas: Five Strokes and the Tumbao</a>
    <p>The drums, how to sit, the five strokes (bass, open, muted, slap, heel-toe) and how they are written, then the tumbao built in six steps with the band: open tones, right hand, left hand, both hands, a cha-cha band and two drums.</p>
  </li>
  <li data-for="all congas" data-topic="latin blues rhythm">
    <a href="watermelon-congas.html">Watermelon Man for Congas</a>
    <p>The tumbao over a 16-bar blues: the form, the break on bar 14, the melody, and the same part in Mongo Santamar&iacute;a's cha-cha and in a boogaloo.</p>
  </li>
  <li data-for="all bass guitar piano drums violin sax other" data-topic="pop harmony">
    <a href="pop-changes.html">Changing the Changes in C, Am, F, G</a>
    <p>The four chords under most pop songs, made richer one move at a time: extensions, passing chords, secondary dominants and ii-V-Is. With a chorus you can build yourself and an ear test.</p>
  </li>
  <li data-for="all guitar" data-topic="pop harmony">
    <a href="pop-changes-guitar.html">Pop Changes for Guitar</a>
    <p>The C, Am, F, G changes as fretboard diagrams: open shapes, extensions, passing chords and secondary dominants.</p>
  </li>
  <li data-for="all piano" data-topic="pop harmony">
    <a href="pop-changes-piano.html">Pop Changes for Piano</a>
    <p>The C, Am, F, G changes with a left-hand root and a right-hand chord, on a keyboard diagram and a grand staff.</p>
  </li>
  <li data-for="all bass" data-topic="pop harmony">
    <a href="pop-changes-bass.html">Pop Changes for Bass: Roots and the Walking Line</a>
    <p>The root of each chord, then the stepwise walking line through the passing chords, in bass clef and on a fretboard.</p>
  </li>
  <li data-for="all guitar" data-topic="harmony">
    <a href="chord-shapes-guitar.html">Guitar Chord Shapes: From Pop and Rock Toward Jazz</a>
    <p>Thirteen steps from open triads and power chords through barre chords, 7ths, shells and top-string triads to drop 2, drop 3 and altered dominants, each with diagrams, a staff and sound.</p>
  </li>
  <li data-for="all guitar" data-topic="harmony">
    <a href="chord-shapes-guitar-hand.html">Guitar Chord Shapes by Hand</a>
    <p>The same chords ordered by what the fretting hand finds hard, from one-finger shapes to barres, muted strings and stretches, with what goes wrong at each step.</p>
  </li>
  <li data-for="all guitar" data-topic="rhythm">
    <a href="hammer-ons-pull-offs.html">Hammer-ons and Pull-offs on Guitar</a>
    <p>From one finger on one string to trills, licks and the Sus embellishment on open D, A and C, each written in notation and tablature that plays.</p>
  </li>
  <li data-for="all guitar" data-topic="pop rhythm">
    <a href="travis-picking.html">Travis Picking on Guitar</a>
    <p>The thumb alone, pinches, fingers between the thumb notes, then C, G, Am and D, chord changes, hammer-ons and pull-offs, and the band. Ends with a note on chicken pickin'.</p>
  </li>
  <li data-for="all piano" data-topic="harmony">
    <a href="chord-shapes-piano.html">Piano Chord Voicings: From Pop Triads Toward Jazz</a>
    <p>Thirteen steps from triads and inversions through slash chords, 7ths, guide tones and shells to rootless, drop 2, spread, quartal and upper-structure voicings.</p>
  </li>
  <li data-for="all piano" data-topic="harmony">
    <a href="chord-shapes-piano-hand.html">Piano Voicings by Hand</a>
    <p>The same voicings ordered by what the hands find hard: span, black keys, two hands together, leaps, stretches and independence.</p>
  </li>
  <li data-for="all guitar piano" data-topic="harmony">
    <a href="inversions.html">Inversions: Root Position, First and Second Inversion</a>
    <p>Major and minor triads with the root, 3rd or 5th in the bass, their figured-bass names (⁶ and ⁶₄) and slash-chord names (C/E, C/G), on piano and guitar.</p>
  </li>
  <li data-for="all voice" data-topic="pop">
    <a href="voice-pop.html">Pop Singing: Speech, Mix, Runs and the Mic</a>
    <p>Breath, onsets, speech-level singing and the mix, words, safe belting, pentatonic runs, cry and flips, phrasing with a mic, and singing a third above. Exercises move into your range.</p>
  </li>
  <li data-for="all voice" data-topic="jazz">
    <a href="voice-jazz.html">Jazz Singing: Swing, Scat and the Changes</a>
    <p>Conversational tone, swing eighths and ghost notes, scat syllables, the blues scale, arpeggios and guide tones through a ii-V-I, back-phrasing a ballad, and trading fours.</p>
  </li>
  <li data-for="all voice" data-topic="reading">
    <a href="voice-classical.html">Classical Singing: Breath, Pure Vowels and Legato</a>
    <p>Appoggio breathing, onset and legato, the five Italian vowels, resonance, registers and the passaggio, the nine-note scale, messa di voce, vibrato, diction and solfège.</p>
  </li>
  <li data-for="all bass guitar piano drums violin sax other" data-topic="pop harmony">
    <a href="four-chord-loops.html">Four-Chord Loops</a>
    <p>The loops under a great many songs (I V vi IV, vi IV I V, the fifties loop, the turnaround, a borrowed chord, two minor loops) one at a time, each on a chart and a staff, with a loop builder and an ear test.</p>
  </li>
  <li data-for="all bass guitar piano drums violin sax other" data-topic="harmony">
    <a href="cadences.html">Cadences, and the One That Is Not</a>
    <p>Authentic, half, deceptive, plagal and backdoor endings, each as a four-bar phrase on a staff, with the argument for why the plagal "Amen" is not a cadence, a phrase builder and two ear tests.</p>
  </li>
  <li data-for="all bass guitar piano violin sax other" data-topic="jazz harmony">
    <a href="guide-tones.html">Guide Tones</a>
    <p>The 3rd and 7th of each chord written as a single line over four-chord loops, a two-five-one and the turnaround. The band plays the line.</p>
  </li>
  <li data-for="all bass guitar piano violin sax other" data-topic="harmony">
    <a href="minor-changes.html">Changes in a Minor Key</a>
    <p>From natural-minor i, iv, v to the harmonic-minor V7, the Picardy third, a walking bass and the ii&deg;-V-i, in A minor.</p>
  </li>
  <li data-for="all bass guitar piano violin sax other" data-topic="pop harmony">
    <a href="borrowed-chords.html">Borrowed Chords</a>
    <p>The minor iv, the &#9837;VII and the &#9837;VI borrowed into a major key, one at a time, with a chord-by-chord builder and an ear test.</p>
  </li>
  <li data-for="all bass guitar piano drums violin sax other" data-topic="jazz harmony">
    <a href="turnarounds.html">Turnarounds and Rhythm Changes</a>
    <p>I-vi-ii-V made richer: sevenths, a dominant on the vi, starting on the iii, tritone substitutions and the first four bars of <em>I Got Rhythm</em>.</p>
  </li>
  <li data-for="all bass guitar piano violin sax other" data-topic="harmony">
    <a href="reharmonize.html">Reharmonizing a Melody</a>
    <p>One tune, <em>Ode to Joy</em>, with four sets of chords under it, played with the melody. Mix the settings two bars at a time.</p>
  </li>
  <li data-for="all bass guitar piano drums other" data-topic="pop jazz latin">
    <a href="arrange-band.html">Arranging 1: Who Plays What in a Band</a>
    <p>The four jobs in a rhythm section, built up one player at a time. Switch players in and out while the band plays and see each part written out.</p>
  </li>
  <li data-for="all bass drums" data-topic="pop jazz latin rhythm">
    <a href="arrange-bass-drums.html">Arranging 2: Bass and Drums</a>
    <p>Why the bass follows the kick, how the groove sets the feel, walking in swing and the tumbao in Latin music.</p>
  </li>
  <li data-for="all guitar piano" data-topic="pop jazz">
    <a href="arrange-chords.html">Arranging 3: Guitar and Keyboards</a>
    <p>Comping: strum patterns, voicing and register, the off-beat chop, jazz comping, and two chord players without a fight.</p>
  </li>
  <li data-for="all piano" data-topic="jazz blues pop">
    <a href="arrange-organ.html">Arranging 4: The Organ</a>
    <p>A playable tonewheel organ: pull the nine tonebars, switch the chorus, work the swell pedal and spin the Leslie, then hear it in the band.</p>
  </li>
  <li data-for="all bass guitar piano drums other" data-topic="pop jazz latin rhythm">
    <a href="patterns/index.html">Accompaniment Patterns</a>
    <p>A lesson for every bass line, comping rhythm, drum groove and conga part the band plays, each built up from simpler ones, played on the band and written out.</p>
  </li>
  <li data-for="all bass guitar piano drums violin sax voice other" data-topic="sound">
    <a href="sound-harmonics.html">Sound 1: The Harmonic Series and Fourier</a>
    <p>The harmonics of a note written out over any root, with how far each is from the piano. Build square, triangle, sawtooth and pulse waves from sine waves.</p>
  </li>
  <li data-for="all bass guitar piano drums violin sax voice other" data-topic="sound">
    <a href="sound-waveforms.html">Sound 2: Oscillators and Pulse-Width Modulation</a>
    <p>The classic synth waves on an oscilloscope and spectrum, pulse width, and PWM.</p>
  </li>
  <li data-for="all bass guitar piano drums violin sax voice other" data-topic="sound">
    <a href="sound-noise.html">Sound 3: Noise</a>
    <p>White, pink and brown noise, and wind, surf, hi-hats, snares and rain made from it.</p>
  </li>
  <li data-for="all bass guitar piano drums violin sax voice other" data-topic="sound">
    <a href="sound-filter.html">Sound 4: Filters</a>
    <p>Low-pass, high-pass, resonance, band-pass, notch and EQ, on noise, music or your own voice.</p>
  </li>
  <li data-for="all bass guitar piano drums violin sax voice other" data-topic="sound">
    <a href="sound-lfo.html">Sound 5: LFOs</a>
    <p>Vibrato, tremolo, wah and auto-pan from one slow oscillator, and what happens when it speeds up.</p>
  </li>
  <li data-for="all bass guitar piano drums violin sax voice other" data-topic="sound">
    <a href="sound-subtractive.html">Sound 6: Subtractive Synthesis</a>
    <p>A two-oscillator synth with filter, envelopes and LFO, played from the keys or MIDI, with presets for bass, brass, pads and plucks.</p>
  </li>
  <li data-for="all bass guitar piano drums violin sax voice other" data-topic="sound">
    <a href="sound-fm.html">Sound 7: FM Synthesis</a>
    <p>Carrier, modulator, ratio and index: sidebands on the spectrum, and bells, electric piano and bass from two sine waves.</p>
  </li>
  <li data-for="all bass guitar piano drums violin sax voice other" data-topic="sound">
    <a href="sound-wavetable.html">Sound 8: Wavetable Synthesis</a>
    <p>Morph through a table of wave shapes by hand or with an LFO.</p>
  </li>
  <li data-for="all bass guitar piano drums violin sax voice other" data-topic="sound">
    <a href="sound-distortion.html">Sound 9: Distortion</a>
    <p>Soft clip, hard clip, tube-like, wavefolder and bit crusher, and the harmonics each one adds.</p>
  </li>
  <li data-for="all bass guitar piano drums violin sax voice other" data-topic="sound">
    <a href="sound-compressor.html">Sound 10: The Compressor</a>
    <p>Threshold, ratio, knee, attack and release, with a live gain-reduction meter.</p>
  </li>
  <li data-for="all bass guitar piano drums violin sax voice other" data-topic="sound">
    <a href="sound-reverb.html">Sound 11: Reverb</a>
    <p>A convolution reverb with a room you build: decay, pre-delay, damping and early reflections.</p>
  </li>
  <li data-for="all bass guitar piano drums violin sax voice other" data-topic="sound">
    <a href="sound-chorus.html">Sound 12: Chorus and Flanger</a>
    <p>Moving short delays, the Doppler effect, and the comb filter.</p>
  </li>
  <li data-for="all bass guitar piano drums violin sax voice other" data-topic="sound">
    <a href="sound-phaser.html">Sound 13: Phaser</a>
    <p>All-pass filters, phase and sweeping notches.</p>
  </li>
  <li data-for="all bass guitar piano drums violin sax voice other" data-topic="sound">
    <a href="sound-vocoder.html">Sound 14: The Vocoder</a>
    <p>Talk into the microphone and play chords: the voice shapes the synth band by band.</p>
  </li>
</ul>

<script>
// Filter the lessons by instrument and topic; the order of the list stays as written. Both choices are kept
// (localStorage.llInst, llTopic) and can be given in the address: lessons/?instrument=bass&topic=blues
(function () {
  var inst = document.getElementById('ll-pick'), topic = document.getElementById('ll-topic'), items = document.querySelectorAll('#ll-list li'), note = document.getElementById('ll-note');
  function valid(group, attr, v) { return v && group.querySelector('button[' + attr + '="' + v + '"]') ? v : 'all'; }
  function has(li, attr, v) { return v === 'all' || li.getAttribute(attr).split(' ').indexOf(v) >= 0; }
  var cur = { inst: 'all', topic: 'all' };
  function show() {
    var n = 0;
    Array.prototype.forEach.call(items, function (li) { var on = has(li, 'data-for', cur.inst) && has(li, 'data-topic', cur.topic); li.hidden = !on; if (on) n++; });
    Array.prototype.forEach.call(inst.querySelectorAll('button'), function (b) { b.setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(b.getAttribute('data-inst') === cur.inst)); });
    Array.prototype.forEach.call(topic.querySelectorAll('button'), function (b) { b.setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(b.getAttribute('data-topic') === cur.topic)); });
    note.hidden = n > 0;
    try { localStorage.setItem('llInst', cur.inst); localStorage.setItem('llTopic', cur.topic); } catch (e) {}
  }
  inst.addEventListener('click', function (e) { var b = e.target.closest('button'); if (b) { cur.inst = b.getAttribute('data-inst'); show(); } });
  topic.addEventListener('click', function (e) { var b = e.target.closest('button'); if (b) { cur.topic = b.getAttribute('data-topic'); show(); } });
  var qi = /[?&]instrument=([a-z]+)/.exec(location.search), qt = /[?&]topic=([a-z]+)/.exec(location.search), si = null, st = null;
  try { si = localStorage.getItem('llInst'); st = localStorage.getItem('llTopic'); } catch (e) {}
  cur.inst = valid(inst, 'data-inst', qi ? qi[1] : si);
  cur.topic = valid(topic, 'data-topic', qt ? qt[1] : st);
  show();
})();
</script>
```
